source_context_translations.translation: A way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; a name that can be named is not the constant Name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route along which people or vehicles travel from one place to another.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This concrete sense denotes a traversable route, not the Laozi’s metaphysical principle.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, formal and literary; also common in received pre-Qin texts
Sentence Translations (English): The great road is very level, yet the people prefer bypaths.
One who governs a state first puts its roads in order.
The road is obstructed and long, so travelers find it difficult to arrive.
The gentleman does not travel by an improper road.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To express something in words, especially by explaining or declaring it aloud.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): As a verb, 道 emphasizes verbal expression or explanation rather than possessing or following a way.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, literary and formal; common in philosophical and historiographical prose
Sentence Translations (English): Those who possessed the ancient way explained it to the multitude.
One who has words states their meaning.
The historian described the ruler’s virtue.
What cannot be stated is not without its principle.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The underlying way or order of reality, contrasted with any particular way that can be verbally stated and thereby limited.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here 道 is the ultimate, ineffable principle rather than a specific route, method, or verbal formulation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi philosophical text in the received Wang Bi recension; an early Classical Chinese conceptual layer transmitted with Wang Bi’s third-century commentary
